clue.text: Change to a nicer garment that is particularly striking

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its form, so the following letters are rearranged

blocks.note: all eight letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Someone swaps into a nicer outfit that turns heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change to' reads as an instruction to dress up, but 'to' belongs in the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A fashion designer's showpiece outfit is called a creation, especially an eye-catching one.

clue.text: Copper starts to suspect traffic officer's methadone habit

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, one taken from each

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the first letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A policeman begins to suspect a traffic cop has a drug habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' invites a police reading alongside the traffic officer, but it is the metal's chemical symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A custom is a habit or established practice, something regularly done.

clue.text: Involve former reservists in line-up

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: the TA was the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force, since renamed
taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting ex-reservists to join a parade formation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line-up' reads as one word for a formation; split, it gives a word written upwards. The Territorial Army became the Army Reserve, hence 'former'.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to involve it as a necessary part or consequence.

clue.text: Vegetable rotation is supported by final 20% of membership

indicators.note: a fifth of a ten-letter word is two letters, and only the last two survive

blocks.note: a turn is a rotation
taken as written

explanation.surface: Crop rotation is backed by a fifth of the members of a growers' club.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, being supported by means the second piece sits beneath the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnip is a root vegetable with a white bulbous root.

clue.text: Expose rogue as incredibly immoderate

indicators.note: something incredible is beyond belief, suggesting the letters are wildly reordered

blocks.note: to out someone is to expose them publicly
these seven letters are the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: Unmask a villain as wildly excessive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' looks like a joining word but its letters are part of the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Outrageous means shockingly excessive, going far beyond what is reasonable or moderate.

clue.text: Flipping games leads to tantrums

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over end to end, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: games such as football and tennis are sports

explanation.surface: Losing at games makes people throw tantrums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' could be a mild British curse word here, but it is the turnaround signal. A strop is a British word for a sulk or fit of temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a strop is British slang for a sulky fit of bad temper, much like a tantrum.

clue.text: Shorten time to dash about at the back

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so only the last letter is kept

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to dash is to run
c, short for circa, means about
taken as written
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: No time to rush around at the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the back' reads as a phrase; 'at' is kept whole and 'the back' gives the end of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: To truncate something is to cut it short by lopping off the end.

clue.text: Degree in golf management

blocks.note: an order is a rank or degree, as in 'of the first order'
taken as written
Golf is G in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone holds a qualification in running golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degree in golf management' reads as a university course; 'in' is used literally.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordering affairs is arranging and organising them, a form of management or control.

clue.text: Parted from Sun journalist over German article

blocks.note: taken as written
der is the masculine form of 'the' in German
ED, short for editor, stands for a journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter quits the Sun tabloid over a piece on Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' here means the journalist comes after the German word; the Sun is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Sundered means split apart or severed, so parted is a synonym.

clue.text: Swamp rat in US ate bananas

indicators.note: going bananas is slang for going crazy, so the letters are scrambled wildly

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rodent in America gobbled up some bananas in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like what the rat ate, but it is the signal to rearrange the letters of rat, US and ate.
explanation.definitionFit: To swamp something is to flood or soak it completely, which is what saturate means as a verb.

clue.text: Load of dye heartlessly dumped in stream

indicators.note: without a heart means the middle letter is removed, leaving only the outside pair
dumping one thing in another puts it inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the word dye with its central letter removed
burn is the Scottish word for a small stream

explanation.surface: A load of dye has been thoughtlessly tipped into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: A burn is a Scots and Northern English word for a brook; the outer letters of dye go into it to make BURDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden is a heavy load that someone carries, literally or figuratively.

clue.text: Gold I trap by a lake is not fake

blocks.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
taken as written
a gin is a snare or trap for animals
taken as written
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone boasts that the gold they caught by a lake is genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold' as OR is a heraldic convention; a gin trap is a spring trap used for catching animals.
explanation.definitionFit: An original is the genuine article rather than a copy or forgery, so it is authentic.

clue.text: Mark's chief executive initially hard to find

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letters, here of each of a pair of words

blocks.note: a scar is a mark left on the skin; the 's here means 'is'
the first letter of each of these two words

explanation.surface: A chief executive named Mark is hard to get hold of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark's' looks like a person's name in the possessive; it is a scar plus 'is' joining it to the next part.
explanation.definitionFit: Something scarce is in short supply, so it is rarely found and difficult to come by.

clue.text: Quiet individual on drugs cartel is opening up

blocks.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction for quiet
I is the single person speaking, an individual
taken as written
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so two of them
a ring is a group of people working together illicitly, like a cartel

explanation.surface: A shy person high on drugs is talking about a drug cartel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening up' looks like confessing, but means breaking new ground. E for ecstasy doubles up for the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Pioneering work opens up a new field, being the first to explore or develop it.

clue.text: Work in secret as an underground movement

indicators.note: to work something is to knead or shape it, so the letters are reshaped

blocks.note: all ten letters of these three words are the raw material

explanation.surface: Operating covertly as a clandestine movement.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads like a description of the Resistance, tempting a cryptic definition, but 'Work' rearranges the next three words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Resistance names the covert networks that fought Nazi occupation in wartime Europe from hiding.

clue.text: Head lied about preceding unemployment

indicators.note: about can mean around or every which way, so the letters move into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a ness is a headland, as in Dungeness

explanation.surface: The boss fibbed about being out of work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' looks like a boss; it is a headland, which a ness is in English place names like Dungeness.
explanation.definitionFit: Idleness is the state of having no work to do, so it can stand for unemployment.

clue.text: It starts with a star's flutter

blocks.note: alpha labels the brightest star in a constellation, as in Alpha Centauri
a flutter is British slang for a small bet

explanation.surface: A celebrity's nervous excitement begins with a little wager.
explanation.walkthrough: A flutter is British slang for a small gamble. The definition is a riddle: the thing that begins with the letter A.
explanation.definitionFit: The English alphabet is the letter sequence whose first member is A.

clue.text: Content to fingerprint rude Russian gatecrasher

indicators.note: the content of something is what it holds, so the letters lie within the following words

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word, all of the second, and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A rude Russian party-crasher is happy to give his fingerprints.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' reads as willing, but it is the noun: what the next words contain.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatecrasher turns up uninvited, so is an intruder at the event.

clue.text: State inquest changes its final direction for offender

indicators.note: the compass point at the end of the word is swapped for its opposite point

blocks.note: Del. is the abbreviation for Delaware, a US state
taken as written

explanation.surface: A government inquest alters its ultimate course in dealing with a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Direction' means a compass point: the final S (south) of the inquest word swaps to N (north). Delaware is a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: A delinquent is a wrongdoer, typically a young person guilty of minor crimes.

clue.text: Fashionable sister does't hesitate to make firm demands

indicators.note: not hesitating means the hesitation noise, the British 'er', is left out

blocks.note: in means fashionable
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trendy sister is quick to make demands.
explanation.walkthrough: Er is the British spelling of the hesitation sound, so a sister who doesn't hesitate loses her ER.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand something forcefully and refuse to back down.

clue.text: Consequence of Ulster struggle

indicators.note: a struggle is a disorderly fight, throwing the letters into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An outcome of the conflict in Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is a name for Northern Ireland, whose Troubles the surface evokes.
explanation.definitionFit: A result is the outcome that follows from an action, the same as a consequence.

clue.text: Regularly sick at finish, after a climb

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: taken as written
the first and third letters of this word
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: Someone is routinely ill at the summit after a hike.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces follow 'a' because of 'after a'; altitude sickness fits the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to go upward, which is what climbing means as a verb.

clue.text: Spur is a feature of Sussex horticulture

indicators.note: a feature of something is part of it, so the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: running across the join of these two words

explanation.surface: A spur, perhaps a garden wall, is typical of gardening in Sussex.
explanation.walkthrough: Sussex is an English county; the letters straddle the end of Sussex and the start of horticulture.
explanation.definitionFit: To spur someone on is to urge or encourage them strongly, which is what exhort means.

clue.text: Invaders reduced by half after nasty winds

indicators.note: halving the word means dropping its first four letters and keeping the rest

blocks.note: mean can mean unkind or nasty
taken as written

explanation.surface: An invading army is cut down by half after nasty winds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winds' looks like the weather noun; it is the verb, as a river winds.
explanation.definitionFit: A river that meanders follows a twisting, looping course, so it winds back and forth.

clue.text: Represent group on the fringes of eco-terrorism

indicators.note: fringes are the outer edges, so only the first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of this word
a body is an organised group of people

explanation.surface: An organisation acts on the margins of environmental extremism.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'group on' the fringes means BODY placed after them.
explanation.definitionFit: To embody an idea is to give it concrete form, so to represent or personify it.

clue.text: Make fun of independent investigator endlessly breaking the law

indicators.note: without an end, so the final letter is cut off
breaking into something gets inside it, so these pieces sit within the other

blocks.note: I is the abbreviation for independent
a dick is slang for a private detective
a rule is a law or regulation

explanation.surface: Mock a freelance detective who keeps flouting the law.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick is old slang for a detective; trimmed to DIC and joined to I, it goes inside RULE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ridicule someone is to mock them, holding them up to derision and laughter.

clue.text: Stitch uterus after an operation

indicators.note: an operation works on something and changes it, so the letters are reworked

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A surgeon sews up a womb following surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Operation' fits the surgical picture perfectly, which hides that it is the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A suture is a surgical stitch used to close a wound or incision.

clue.text: Upset a barrier protecting Italian diamonds

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding and guarding it, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a gate is a barrier across an opening
It. is the abbreviation for Italian
D is the card-playing abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: An Italian is upset that a fence is guarding his diamonds.
explanation.walkthrough: D for diamonds is the card-suit abbreviation; 'Upset' looks like wordplay but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being upset in the sense of flustered and nervous is the same as being agitated.
